title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
abstract: arXiv:2610.33536v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Financial fraud caused over \$15.9 billion in losses in the United States in 2025, according to the Federal Trade Commission~\citep{ftc2026databook}. Understanding such large-scale harm requires jointly modeling informational and financial dynamics. Yet existing simulators typically capture only one side of this interaction, leaving a gap in modeling how fraud unfolds in the real world. To bridge this gap, we introduce \textsc{FraudSociety}, the first LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models these coupled dynamics. It integrates a dynamic social environment for information exposure and communication, persistent financial ledgers that preserve payment and loss histories, and a Need-Intent-Action architecture for civilian decision making. translated_title: FraudSociety：一个面向金融诈骗经济的生成式智能体社会
translated_abstract: 根据美国联邦贸易委员会的数据，2025年金融诈骗在美国造成了超过159亿美元的损失。理解如此大规模的危害需要同时对信息动态和金融动态进行联合建模。然而，现有的模拟器通常只能捕捉这种交互的一个方面，在对现实世界中诈骗如何展开的建模上存在空白。为了填补这一空白，我们提出了FraudSociety，这是首个基于LLM智能体、能够联合建模这两种耦合动态的模拟器。它集成了一个用于信息暴露和沟通的动态社会环境、保存支付和损失记录的持久金融账本，以及用于民众决策的“需求-意图-行动”架构。诈骗者还会根据个体的交互历史和账本状态调整其沟通方式和金融行动，从而在两种动态之间形成闭环反馈。
tldr: 该论文提出了首个基于LLM智能体的模拟器FraudSociety，通过联合建模信息动态与金融动态的闭环反馈，以及持久账本和需求-意图-行动架构，来模拟真实世界的金融诈骗经济。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces FraudSociety, the first LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models coupled informational and financial dynamics—featuring a dynamic social environment, persistent financial ledgers, and a Need-Intent-Action architecture—to simulate how financial fraud unfolds in the real world.
